item.title: ‘Cali Fund’ aiming to raise billions for nature receives first donation – of just $1,000
item.description: A major biodiversity fund – which could, in theory, generate billions of dollars annually for conservation – received its first donation of just US$1,000 in November.

item.title: Even ‘weak’ cyclones are being turned into deadly rainmakers by fast-warming oceans
item.description: Despite accurate forecasts, weak cyclones in South Asia triggered deadly floods – highlighting how warmer oceans are amplifying rainfall and reshaping cyclone risks in a warming climate.

item.title: Japan clears hurdle to restart world’s largest nuclear power plant
item.description: Local assembly backs pro-restart governor, paving way for Kashiwazaki-Kariwa’s return nearly 15 years after Fukushima disaster.

item.title: ‘They invite us to speak, but not to decide’
item.description: There was no shortage of Indigenous representatives at COP30, but the conference did not always seem to be listening, writes Dunio Chiriap Jimbicti.

item.title: Hanwha Ocean lands $1.8 billion offshore wind contract as South Korea ramps up wind push
item.description: The 390-MW Shinan Ui project advances after years of delays amid government reforms to speed approvals and boost renewables.

item.title: Trump’s funding cuts for climate agencies ‘a huge disservice’ to Americans and the world, expert warns
item.description: China’s leadership in green technology production and financing could be supported by the opening of a United Nations climate campus in the country, the sustainable development expert and economist told Eco-Business.

item.title: Taiwan opens first hydrogen refuelling stations in test of clean fuel push
item.description: State-run CPC and Linde LienHwa launch pilot sites in Kaohsiung as government weighs hydrogen’s role in energy transition.

item.title: How climate change reshaped the wild in 2025
item.description: Around the world, rising temperatures and erratic weather are forcing animals to adapt in startling ways – with consequences for people and ecosystems alike.

item.title: How insurance can transform our resilience to climate shocks
item.description: From Hurricane Melissa in the Caribbean to floods in Southeast Asia, insurance is an underused tool for adaptation to climate extremes.

item.title: South Korea targets 30 per cent cut in plastic waste by 2030
item.description: A new government roadmap raises levies and curbs single-use plastics, but critics say it ignores production cuts.
